context:
Goal: a question with a large trade-off reaches you with a better option on the table.
Problem (goal): you asked on Nov 8 whether large trade-offs between a question's choices could trigger an option judge to push back. The lane measured it: a rule that counts ruling-and-open-gap losses as large catches item 416 (3 of 3), but sends back 10 of 163 past items you answered with a listed option (6.1%) and catches 1 of 33 otherwise answered. That is not near zero, so the judge was not built. The 416 kind may need the writer to add a third option, not a judge. The lane waits on your pick.
Based on (measured): the lane's run, 11:41 CST Nov 8; #2173 keeps the rule as built (0 of 196).
Departs from: main has no option pushback at all — a adds a writing rule; b leaves main as it is.
Meanwhile: the lane (prose-guard-2) waits for your pick.

options.gain: Catches the kind of question you asked about, without sending good questions back.
options.how: The session that writes a question must offer a better-solution option when its first two options trade off heavily. No judge sends the question back.
options.label: The question writer adds a third option when the trade-offs are large (recommended)
options.lose: The writing rule is on the writer to follow; nothing checks it.

options.how: No pushback and no new writing rule. The lane stops.
options.label: Drop the option judge idea
options.lose: A question with a large trade-off still reaches you with no better option offered.

reply: Filed 13:23 CST: your 743 a is ruling own-743-a-writer-third-option. The question writer adds a third option when trade-offs are large. No judge. The lane builds the writing rule.
short: Option judge, or the writer adds a third option?

shown.label: The question writer adds a third option when the trade-offs are large (recommended)

title: When a question's options trade off heavily, should a judge push back, or should the question writer add a better third option?
why: The lane waits on your pick between the two designs.
